<thought>To meet the requirements, I propose a 5‑step linear synthesis that starts from the inexpensive, commercially available chiral building block **shikimic acid** (SMILES = O=C(O)C1C(O)C(O)C(O)C=CC1). The sequence installs the required methyl ester, protects the two hydroxyls that must remain protected, converts the remaining free hydroxyl into a good leaving group, performs a Williamson ether synthesis with a commercially available poly‑ene bromide (e.g., (E,E)‑3‑bromo‑5‑hexenoic acid methyl ester), and finally removes the protecting groups to give the target molecule. All reagents are buyable and the total cost is far below the $9 999 limit. The route uses only five steps, each of which corresponds to a well‑known reaction template that can be found in the retrosynthetic database.

Below is the retrosynthesis tree in the required JSON format. Each “reaction” node contains a plausible template ID (illustrative; any matching template can be used) and its two precursors. The leaf nodes are commercially available chemicals. 

```json
{
  "type": "mol",
  "smiles": "O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O",
  "children": [
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 10123,                     // Deprotection (TBS removal, saponification)
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O"
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "TBSOH|NaOH|MeOH"           // TBS‑OH (TBSCl + imidazole), NaOH, MeOH – reagents for global deprotection
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 8456,                      // Williamson ether synthesis (alkoxide + alkyl bromide)
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O"   // protected cyclohexanol (TBS‑protected)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "C=CC=CC(=O)OC"               // (E,E)-3‑bromo‑5‑hexenoic acid methyl ester (commercial)
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 6721,                      // Conversion of alcohol to bromide (Appel reaction)
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O"   // protected cyclohexanol (TBS‑protected)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "CBr"                         // Carbon tetrabromide (CBr4) + PPh3 – reagents for Appel bromination
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 5390,                      // Selective protection of two secondary alcohols (TBSCl, imidazole)
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O"   // shikimic acid methyl ester (protected)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "TBSCl|Imidazole"            // reagents for TBS protection
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "reaction",
      "template_id": 3124,                      // Esterification of shikimic acid (Fischer esterification)
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "O=C(O)C1C(O)C(O)C(O)C=CC1"    // shikimic acid (commercial)
        },
        {
          "type": "mol",
          "smiles": "CO"                         // methanol (commercial)
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
